whatTheWritePathSaysToday.theShortCircuitThatConstrainsTheDesign: processCityPage tests `city.ruled` BEFORE it reads the zoningDistrict cell. P-326 measured the consequence and left it as a named defect: for a no-table city the district is never consulted, so a district-less parcel and a districted parcel are written the SAME unaccounted cell. P-300's design therefore cannot be a change to buildNoRuledTableCells alone -- the branch has to read the zoning rail, or read a classification table that already encodes the answer. Both halves of this lane (the classification table and the router) exist because of that short-circuit.
whatTheWritePathSaysToday.theP256Guard: assertNoFalseAbsence refuses the whole batch if any cell is kind='absent-verified'. Class (c) is `absent-verified` BY RULING, so this guard must learn the difference between an unearned absence (this job guessing) and an earned one (a class (c) row whose basis names the ordinance that was read). The dispatch states this explicitly: 'a class (c) absence carries what was checked, or it does not ship.'
whatTheWritePathSaysToday.theWriteGate: setbackCellMayBeMoved releases kind='unaccounted' plus this job's own false absences. Every cell this lane writes that is not `unaccounted` (refused, absent-verified, value) is therefore STICKY: a later correction cannot move it. That makes the classification's correctness load-bearing in a way a normal write is not, and is the strongest argument for refusing to guess a class.

item1_classificationTable.shape: One committed JSON row per city: { jurisdictionKey, cityName, countyFips[], class: 'a'|'b'|'c'|null, parcels, ordinanceSection, citationUrl, readAt, evidenceQuote, defaults: {front_ft, rear_ft, side_ft, side_corner_ft} | null, platDisclosure }
item1_classificationTable.whereItLives: hauska-factory, beside the router (src/lib/setback-writer/), so the writer reads ONE table and keeps no second list -- the dispatch's explicit requirement.
item1_classificationTable.rule: class null means unclassified-at-source and the writer leaves the parcel `unaccounted`, named and reported. It is never guessed into a class (dispatch: 'A city you cannot classify at source stays unaccounted, named, and is reported. It is never guessed into a class.').
item1_classificationTable.whyNotInTheCorpus: the class is a fact about the CITY's ordinance and its acquired layers, not about a setback value; (a) and (c) produce no values at all, so the corpus (which is a value corpus) is the wrong home for them. Only (b)'s default row belongs in the corpus.

item2_corpusDefaultRows.shape: A new row kind on SetbackDistrict, marked (proposed field: row_kind: 'jurisdiction-default' | 'district'), with the plat disclosure carried in the row's provenance note and in the corpus table's note. It is NOT a district_name the router could match, so a district code can never resolve to it.
item2_corpusDefaultRows.schemaWork: schema.json and table-types.ts both need the new field; schema.json's district has additionalProperties:false so an unmarked field would fail validation. G7 (max_height_ft sentinel) needs no change: a default row still carries max_height_ft and the same sentinel rule applies to it. G4 (district coverage) must be told that the default row is not a district, or a jurisdiction with a default and no expectedDistricts would read as a coverage miss.
item2_corpusDefaultRows.versionBump: minor bump 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 (new row kind, no existing value changes). The bump is declared here and NOT executed: publishing the corpus is the seat's, per the dispatch.

item3_router.rule: resolveSetbackForParcel(jurisdictionKey, districtCode) keeps its meaning for a parcel WITH a district on file: a code that misses the table stays a miss and never falls through to the default (that is ruling 6's case). A new, separately named entry point resolves the DEFAULT for a jurisdiction, and the writer calls it ONLY on the no-district-on-file path.
item3_router.whyTwoFunctionsAndNotOneFallback: a single function that falls back to the default on a miss would silently convert every district-miss into a default value -- the precise failure A-224 exists to prevent. Two names make the two cases distinguishable in a diff and testable apart, which the dispatch asks for ('Show the two cases apart').

item4_cells.district-miss: kind='refused', reason names the district code AND the city and says to verify with the city; basis keeps codeClass='district-miss' and the router finding. Coupled to P-346 by the ledger policy.
item4_cells.class-a: kind='refused', reason names the city and says the zoning district was not acquired and to verify with the city; basis carries the classification row's citationUrl/section/readAt so the refusal names what was actually read. Coupled to P-364.
item4_cells.class-b: kind='value' on the four rails from the jurisdiction-default row, with the plat disclosure in the cell's reason/basis and the corpus default row as the source; the companion row carries the disclosure and the default's section.
item4_cells.class-c: kind='absent-verified', basis names the ordinance read and that it sets no city-wide line. This is the ONLY branch in this job that can legitimately produce absent-verified, and assertNoFalseAbsence must be narrowed to allow it while still refusing any other absent-verified cell.
item4_cells.unclassified: kind='unaccounted', reason names the city and says it is unclassified at source; reported, never guessed.

item5_ledgerPolicy.change: accept exactly two refusal signatures on the five setback rails: ruling 6's district miss and A-224's zoning-not-acquired. Each matched by its exact reason signature, not by 'refused'. Self-test gains a case per accepted signature and a case proving a differently worded refusal is still rejected.
